title: Why some volcanoes explode and others ooze lava
group: HOWN — How and Why in Nature
examples: Why is Hawaiian lava so runny?

figure.name: x-compare
figure.verdict: Stickier magma traps gas, so it explodes

explain.say: Volcanoes erupt in two main ways. Some, like those in Hawaii, pour out rivers of glowing lava, while others, like Mount St Helens, blow apart in huge explosions.

draw.text: Why some volcanoes explode and others ooze lava

explain.say: Now let me show you the real thing in 3D: inside a volcano. Look at the ash cloud, the crater and the lava flow. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.

draw.text: Why some volcanoes explode and others ooze lava

explain.say: The difference is how sticky the magma is. Basalt magma has little silica and is very hot, so it is runny, and gas bubbles slip out gently.

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: Stickier magma traps gas, so it explodes

explain.say: Magma rich in silica is thick and sticky, like cold toothpaste. Gas cannot escape, so pressure builds until the magma shatters into ash and blasts out.

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: Stickier magma traps gas, so it explodes

explain.say: So the rule is simple: the stickier the magma and the more gas it holds, the more explosive the eruption. Runny lava builds wide gentle shield volcanoes; sticky magma builds steep cones.

faq.a: Their magma is thick and sticky because it has lots of silica. Gas bubbles cannot escape, pressure builds up, and the magma bursts apart into ash and rock in an explosion.
asks: Why did Mount St Helens blow up?

faq.q: Why is Hawaiian lava so runny?
faq.a: Hawaiian lava is basalt, which has little silica and is very hot, about 1,100 to 1,200 degrees Celsius. That makes it flow easily, and gas escapes gently instead of exploding.
asks: Why does some lava flow like a river?

faq.a: Viscosity means how thick and sticky a liquid is. Honey has high viscosity and water low. In magma, more silica means higher viscosity and more explosive eruptions.
A shield volcano is a wide volcano with gentle slopes, built from many flows of runny lava. Mauna Loa in Hawaii is a shield volcano and one of the biggest on Earth.
asks: What shape are runny lava volcanoes?

faq.a: Volcanic ash is not burnt material. It is tiny pieces of shattered rock and glass made when sticky, gassy magma explodes. It can travel thousands of kilometres and is dangerous to planes.

facts: Basalt lava erupts at about 1,100 to 1,200 degrees Celsius.
Mount St Helens in the USA erupted explosively on 18 May 1980.
Mauna Loa in Hawaii is a shield volcano built by runny basalt lava.

quiz.say: Which magma is most likely to cause an explosive eruption?

options.show: Thick, sticky and full of gas
options.say: Thick, sticky and full of gas

quiz.why: Sticky magma traps gas bubbles, so pressure builds until the magma bursts apart.

wrong.1: Runny magma lets gas escape, so it oozes out gently.
wrong.2: Solid rock does not erupt at all.
